response:
Diagnosis: the frontier now has two distinguishable optima and generation 6 clarified how to move along it. Alpha precision is maximized by devices that stabilize the *accrual* signal or discard uninformative firms: three-year smoothing (α 6.2%, t 5.26), the absolute stability gate (α 5.0%, t 5.41, and it also lifted FMB to 3.62 — the first device to help both), and the long-side restriction (α 5.2%, t 5.22, confirming the payoff is on the cash-backed side, since the mirror short-side version gave only 1.2%). Cross-sectional slope is maximized by industry demeaning plus a two-channel durability weight (FMB 4.42, Sharpe 0.42) at the cost of ~1.5pp of alpha. Notably, the *hard absolute gate* dominated the continuous rank weight on both t-alpha and FMB, which says the amplifier is an economic threshold ("earnings are genuinely stable") rather than a relative ordering. This batch therefore crosses the alpha-side devices with the FMB-side device, and explores two untested measurement channels (sales-scaled accruals, manipulation-resistant gross-profit stability).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: IndustryAccrualsGatedByStabilityThreshold
EXPRESSION: MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(RANK(IND_ADJ(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), SUB(at, che)), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), SUB(at, che))))))), INDICATOR(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 5)), -0.05))
HYPOTHESIS: Among firms that clear an absolute standard of earnings stability, peer-relative accrual restraint is the cleanest available marker of cash-backed profit; firms failing the stability standard carry no accrual information at all.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The absolute stability gate is the only device so far that improved both metrics simultaneously (t-alpha 5.41, FMB 3.62), and industry demeaning is the only device that reliably pushes FMB above 4.2, so crossing them targets the archive's unmet objective of strong cross-sectional and portfolio evidence together. Neither modification touches the other's economic content — one selects the sample, the other normalizes the ranking variable.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: ChronicAccrualsGatedByStabilityThreshold
EXPRESSION: MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(RANK(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), SUB(at, che)), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), SUB(at, che))), 3)))), INDICATOR(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 5)), -0.05))
HYPOTHESIS: Sustained accrual restraint, evaluated only within the population of genuinely stable-earnings firms, is the purest empirical statement of the theme's economic story.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Three-year smoothing produced the largest alpha in the archive (6.2%) and the absolute stability gate produced the highest t-alpha per unit of alpha, and both operate on different objects (the accrual time series versus sample selection), so their effects should be close to additive. This is the most direct attempt to push alpha above 6% while keeping the FMB slope above 3.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: StabilityGatedAccrualsWeightedByEarningsFloor
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), SUB(at, che)), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), SUB(at, che)))))), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ni, at), 5))), INDICATOR(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 5)), -0.05))
HYPOTHESIS: Durability has a dispersion requirement and a level requirement: a firm must not swing (absolute volatility gate) and must remain profitable at its worst (continuous floor weight), and only then does low accrual content identify genuinely cash-backed performance.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The two quality channels enter in the functional forms each performed best in — volatility as a hard economic threshold and worst-year ROA as a continuous rank that produced FMB above 4 — rather than being averaged into a single index, which is what diluted alpha in the gen 4 and gen 6 composite weights. It tests whether a hybrid hard/soft conditioning structure dominates either pure form.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: ChronicCashBackedLongSideOnly
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(RANK(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), SUB(at, che)), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), SUB(at, che))), 3)))), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 5)))), INDICATOR(NEG(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), SUB(at, che)), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), SUB(at, che))), 3)), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: The premium accrues to firms whose operating cash flow has persistently exceeded reported earnings; grading only that population and treating all others as neutral should give the sharpest portfolio spread.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen 6 long-side restriction and three-year smoothing each independently improved the portfolio evidence (t-alpha 5.22 and 5.26), and both derive from the same finding that the alpha is generated by chronically cash-backed firms rather than by shorting accrual inflators. Combining them tests whether persistence of cash backing, measured only where it exists, is the sharpest version of the mechanism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: SalesScaledAccrualsGatedByStability
EXPRESSION: MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), sale), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), sale)))), INDICATOR(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 5)), -0.05))
HYPOTHESIS: Accrual distortion is best measured per dollar of revenue, since revenue is the base against which receivables and inventory recognition decisions are actually made, and asset-scaled accruals conflate discretion with capital intensity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every accrual leg in the archive is scaled by net operating assets, so the scaling choice has never been tested against a revenue base even though the earlier working-capital-to-sales experiment showed the sales denominator carries independent information (FMB 2.54). Pairing it with the proven stability gate holds the conditioning structure fixed so the scaling decision is cleanly identified.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: AccrualsTimesGrossProfitStability
EXPRESSION: MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), SUB(at, che)), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), SUB(at, che)))))), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Stability should be measured on the least manipulable line of the income statement: a firm with a steady gross profit stream has genuinely durable economics, whereas steady net income can itself be the product of the accrual smoothing this signal is trying to detect.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Conditioning on net-income stability is partly circular — accruals are the tool used to make net income look stable — so replacing it with gross-profit stability removes a mechanical link between the two legs and should produce a cleaner interaction if the story is economic rather than mechanical. Gross profit is available for the full sample, so coverage should match the leaders.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
